question: Can stable sorting into two symbol classes itself explain a readable ordered word shape?

teaching_example.claim: With only these two stable subsequences all six original orders collide.

general_argument: For fixed disjoint-class subsequences of lengths k and n-k, each choice of the k A positions yields exactly one distinct source sequence. Hence there are binom(n,k) possible interleavings. A lossless unrestricted writer must retain enough information somewhere to distinguish them.
conditional_limits: Bound assumes every interleaving is allowed, no external dictionary/grammar/context restriction.
Restricting permissible source words can reduce the ambiguity; must specify those restrictions, not claim impossible readable sorting universally.
Information can be represented by explicit signs, spatial placement, context or restricted lexical knowledge; no fixed added glyph count is established.
No native sound, character class, morpheme, word value or alphabet selected.

predecessor_distinction.IDEA000929: Each original symbol contributes one row and one column coordinate; equal-length streams pair by known indices. Not the same information loss as sorting source symbols into disjoint classes. Fixed native929motif contradiction remains unchanged.
predecessor_distinction.IDEA000932: Source spatial attachment can retain ordering but its native binding remains unsupported.
predecessor_distinction.GDT1202: Any fixed deterministic, lossless one-source-token/one-written-group code preserves word equality and frequency partition. Permutation plus a uniquely recoverable mask does not fix prior four-source frequency failures. Other source languages or grouping contracts not excluded.

decision: No encoder or fresh frequency run. Pure unmarked stable partition is not a complete unrestricted reversible writer; a paid repair would still require a decision-changing source/grouping or spelling-choice account. No new supported Voynich mechanism.
